title: The Late Bid
delivery: Liam narrator-led; dry amusement becomes suspicion, then controlled triumph
description:
Lucia steals an auction paddle while Jason eyes a painting that could clear their debt. Then she notices tomorrow's date on tonight's bid sheet.

Original GTA VI fan fiction | Narration: Liam via ElevenLabs / 11.ai

story_audit.goal: Recover the real stolen canvas as leverage to cancel the Fixer's debt.
story_audit.stakes: Their fingerprints and Jason's address will turn them into disposable suspects.
story_audit.obstacle: The auction is a staged frame-up; Jason wants to destroy the apparent prize.
story_audit.planted_clue: Tomorrow's date in fresh ink on the bid sheet; painting addressed to Jason.
story_audit.payoff: An impossible high bid provokes the buyer to reach behind his chair, revealing where he concealed the original.
story_audit.causal_check: Date creates suspicion; shipping label proves target; false bid threatens buyer's control; reflex exposes real prize; original buys debt cancellation, demand sent rather than magically accepted.

canon_status: Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are GTA VI characters in fan-art adaptation. The Fixer is an original supporting character. All plots, jobs, props, businesses and scene-specific sets here are invented noncanon fan fiction.
script: Lucia stole the auction paddle because stealing the painting would get Jason killed before sunrise. The Fixer owned their debt. Tonight, his secret buyer was collecting a stolen canvas as payment. Jason wanted to slash it. Lucia noticed wet ink on the buyer's bid sheet: tomorrow's date. The auction had already happened. Tonight was a rehearsal, with their fingerprints supplying the missing thieves. Jason called her paranoid. Then she turned the canvas over: its shipping label named his apartment. Lucia took the paddle into the glass booth and raised the buyer's ceiling by two million. He panicked, reached for the emergency cancellation key, and exposed the original painting behind his chair. They left the fake, took the original, and sent the Fixer one offer: their debt, cancelled.
